# CSVs
assessments_df            <- read_csv("assessments.csv")
opa_properties_public2_df <- read_csv("opa_properties_public-2.csv")

pwd_parcels_sf            <- st_read("PWD_PARCELS.geojson")

```{r print-colunmns} 
# =============================================================================
# 4. Data Cleaning & Data Processing
# =============================================================================

pud <- opa_properties_public2_df  # use the public properties dataset
options(scipen = 999)
str(pud)

pud <- pud %>%
  mutate(
    sale_date = as.Date(sale_date, format="%Y-%m-%d"),
    sale_date = if_else(sale_date <= Sys.Date(), sale_date, NA_Date_),
    sale_year = year(sale_date),
    sale_month = month(sale_date),
    sale_quarter = quarter(sale_date),
    days_since_2000 = as.numeric(sale_date - as.Date("2000-01-01"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sale_date))

```


```{r}

# =============================================================================
# 5. Initial Feature Selection
# =============================================================================
useful_features <- pud %>%
  select(
    objectid,
    market_value,
    total_livable_area,
    total_area,
    year_built,
    number_of_bathrooms,
    number_of_bedrooms,
    number_stories,
    garage_spaces,
    exterior_condition,
    interior_condition,
    quality_grade,
    geographic_ward,
    zip_code,
    census_tract,
    location,
    zoning,
    category_code,
    sale_price,
    sale_date,
    fireplaces
  )

```

```{r}

# =============================================================================
# 6. Logical Filtering & Data Cleaning
# =============================================================================
cleaned_features <- useful_features %>%
  filter(
    number_of_bathrooms > 0 & number_of_bathrooms <= 7,
    number_of_bedrooms > 0 & number_of_bedrooms <= 10,
    number_stories > 0 & number_stories <= 5,
    total_livable_area >= 300 & total_livable_area <= 6000,
    total_area >= total_livable_area,
    total_area <= 20000,
    exterior_condition >= 1 & exterior_condition <= 7,
    interior_condition >= 1 & interior_condition <= 7,
    year_built >= 1700 & year_built <= 2023,
    sale_price >= 10000 & sale_price <= 5000000,
    market_value >= 10000 & market_value <= 5000000,
    number_of_bathrooms <= number_of_bedrooms * 2
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    quality_grade = case_when(
      quality_grade == "X" ~ "Highest",
      quality_grade %in% c("X-", "A+", "A", "A-") ~ "High",
      quality_grade %in% c("C", "D", "D-", "D+", "6", "D-", "E", "C-", "E-", "E+") ~ "Lowest",
      TRUE ~ "Mid"
    )
  )


# =============================================================================
# 7. Exclude Bundled Sales & Extreme Outliers
# =============================================================================
filtered_data <- cleaned_features %>% 
  filter(sale_price > 1000)

bundled_ids <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(sale_date, sale_price) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  pull(objectid)

filtered_data <- filtered_data %>% 
  filter(!(objectid %in% bundled_ids))


# =============================================================================
# 8. Create Time-Based Feature (Recency)
# =============================================================================
filtered_data <- filtered_data %>%
  mutate(
    sale_year = year(sale_date),
    current_year = 2023,
    years_since_sale = current_year - sale_year
  )


```


```{r}

# =============================================================================
# 9. Basic Feature Engineering
# =============================================================================
engineered_features <- filtered_data %>%
  # Ensure condition variables are numeric
  mutate(
    exterior_condition = as.numeric(exterior_condition),
    interior_condition = as.numeric(interior_condition)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log_livable_area = log(total_livable_area),
    log_total_area = log(total_area),
    area_ratio = total_livable_area / total_area,
    bathrooms_per_area = number_of_bathrooms / total_livable_area,
    bedrooms_per_area = number_of_bedrooms / total_livable_area,
    exterior_condition_reversed = 8 - exterior_condition,
    interior_condition_reversed = 8 - interior_condition,
    overall_condition = (exterior_condition_reversed + interior_condition_reversed) / 2,
    building_age = current_year - year_built,
    age_category = case_when(
      building_age < 20 ~ "New",
      building_age < 50 ~ "Modern",
      building_age < 100 ~ "Vintage",
      TRUE ~ "Historic"
    ),
    price_per_sqft = sale_price / total_livable_area,
    zip_factor = as.factor(zip_code),
    ward_factor = as.factor(geographic_ward)
  )

# =============================================================================
# 10. Interaction Terms & Derived Variables
# =============================================================================
engineered_features <- engineered_features %>%
  mutate(
    area_zip_interaction = scale(log_livable_area) * as.numeric(as.factor(zip_code)),
    condition_age_interaction = scale(overall_condition) * scale(building_age),
    area_quality_interaction = scale(log_livable_area) * 
      case_when(
        quality_grade == "Highest" ~ 4,
        quality_grade == "High" ~ 3,
        quality_grade == "Mid" ~ 2,
        TRUE ~ 1
      ),
    bath_bed_interaction = scale(number_of_bathrooms) * scale(number_of_bedrooms),
    area_condition_interaction = scale(log_livable_area) * scale(overall_condition)
  )

# =============================================================================
# 11. Final Feature Engineering Refinements
# =============================================================================
engineered_features <- engineered_features %>%
  mutate(
    quality_grade_simplified = case_when(
      quality_grade %in% c("Highest", "High") ~ "High",
      quality_grade == "Mid" ~ "Mid",
      TRUE ~ "Low"
    ),
    quality_adjusted_area = total_livable_area * 
      case_when(
        quality_grade_simplified == "High" ~ 1.4,
        quality_grade_simplified == "Mid" ~ 1.1,
        TRUE ~ 1.0
      ),
    quality_condition_score = overall_condition * 
      case_when(
        quality_grade_simplified == "High" ~ 1.2,
        quality_grade_simplified == "Mid" ~ 1.1,
        TRUE ~ 1.0
      )
  )

# Remove empty strings, NAs, and problematic numeric entries
engineered_features <- engineered_features %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~na_if(., ""))) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.)) %>%
  filter(if_all(where(is.numeric), ~!is.nan(.) & !is.infinite(.)))


```




```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 12. Final Feature Selection for Modeling
# =============================================================================
# Instead of selecting only objectid and sale_price, include a set of predictors for modeling.
final_data <- engineered_features %>%
  select(
    objectid,
    sale_price,
    log_livable_area,
    number_of_bathrooms,
    number_of_bedrooms,
    fireplaces,
    year_built,
    years_since_sale,
    building_age,
    area_ratio,
    price_per_sqft,
    overall_condition,
    quality_adjusted_area,
    bath_bed_interaction
  )

str(final_data)

# (Optional) Save the final dataset for future use
write.csv(final_data, "cleaned_philadelphia_properties_for_modeling.csv", row.names = FALSE)



```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 13. Modeling
# =============================================================================
# Fit a linear model predicting log(sale_price) using the selected engineered features.
model_sale <- lm(log(sale_price) ~ log_livable_area + number_of_bathrooms +
                   number_of_bedrooms + fireplaces + year_built +
                   years_since_sale + building_age + area_ratio + price_per_sqft +
                   overall_condition + quality_adjusted_area + bath_bed_interaction, 
                 data = final_data)
summary(model_sale)

```










```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 14. Modeling Part 2 w/ Spline Transformation 
# =============================================================================

# this is a model with spline transformations on log_livable_area and year_built
model_sale_spline <- lm(log(sale_price) ~ 
                          ns(log_livable_area, df = 4) +    # spline on log_livable_area
                          number_of_bathrooms + 
                          number_of_bedrooms + 
                          fireplaces + 
                          ns(year_built, df = 4) +           # spline on year_built
                          years_since_sale + 
                          building_age + 
                          area_ratio + 
                          price_per_sqft +
                          overall_condition + 
                          quality_adjusted_area + 
                          bath_bed_interaction, 
                        data = final_data)

summary(model_sale_spline)


# Splines were used in this project to flexibly capture non-linear relationships between key predictors (like log_livable_area and year_built) and sale_price. This approach allows the model to adjust for curvature in the data without resorting to overly complex high-degree polynomials, thereby improving fit and predictive accuracy while maintaining interpretability.

```


# EDA Visualizations 

```{r}

# Histogram of sale_price
ggplot(final_data, aes(x = sale_price)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Sale Price", x = "Sale Price", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# Histogram of log(sale_price)
ggplot(final_data, aes(x = log(sale_price))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "darkgreen", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Log(Sale Price)", x = "Log(Sale Price)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# These histograms illustrate how the raw sale prices are heavily right‐skewed, with most properties clustered at lower price ranges and a long tail of high‐value sales. Once you apply a log transformation, the distribution becomes more symmetric and bell‐shaped, indicating that taking the logarithm helps normalize the data for better modeling and analysis.

```



```{r}
# Scatterplot: Sale Price vs. Log(Livable Area)
ggplot(final_data, aes(x = log_livable_area, y = sale_price)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Sale Price vs. Log(Livable Area)", x = "Log(Livable Area)", y = "Sale Price") +
  theme_minimal()

# Scatterplot: Log(Sale Price) vs. Log(Livable Area)
ggplot(final_data, aes(x = log_livable_area, y = log(sale_price))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Log(Sale Price) vs. Log(Livable Area)", x = "Log(Livable Area)", y = "Log(Sale Price)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Scatterplot: Sale Price vs. Year Built with loess smoother
ggplot(final_data, aes(x = year_built, y = sale_price)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Sale Price vs. Year Built", x = "Year Built", y = "Sale Price") +
  theme_minimal()



```


```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, fig.align='center'}

my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("purple4", "blue4", "red4"))(100)


num_vars <- final_data %>%
  select(sale_price, log_livable_area, number_of_bathrooms, number_of_bedrooms,
         fireplaces, year_built, years_since_sale, building_age, area_ratio,
         price_per_sqft, overall_condition, quality_adjusted_area, bath_bed_interaction)


corr_mat <- cor(num_vars, use = "complete.obs")


corrplot(corr_mat, method = "number", type = "upper", 
         tl.cex = 0.8, number.cex = 0.7,
         col = my_palette,
         title = "Correlation Matrix of Model Variables", 
         mar = c(1, 1, 4, 1))

# This correlation matrix displays the linear associations among key numeric variables. It shows that variables like log_livable_area and number_of_bathrooms tend to be strongly positively correlated with sale_price, while indicators such as building_age have an expected inverse relationship. This visualization helps identify potential redundancy among predictors and assess which factors most strongly influence property sale prices.

```
